sermon.title: Overlooked Future Intervention
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Overlooked Future Intervention,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches Isaiah 2:4 and Micah 4 and says a future global intervention by God will end war through the terror of the Lord, as seen on a smaller scale with Jehoshaphat, Jacob and Solomon. He reads Isaiah 2:5-22 on the proud being humbled in that day, and Hebrews 12:26-28 on the shaking of created things, and says man-made doctrines and lifestyles need to be shaken.

Editor note: he says “Matthew 7:7” for “In vain they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men,” which is Mark 7:7 (also Matthew 15:9). The captions garble several names and words, corrected where the Bible passage is clear (Dagon in 1 Samuel 5, Ananias and Sapphira in Acts 5, Shintoism, Wicca, Mount Sinai, and “George Butch” read as Bush because he names Bush in the same passage); the date list “’50s … ’90s” is garbled and shown with [unclear]. Names of several other preachers are garbled in the captions (shown as [unclear] and not guessed), and the captions give “Jake” for a minister. He quotes 1 Samuel 5, Matthew 19, Psalm 92:13, Psalm 92, Romans 14:17 and 2 Kings 19 without naming the references. He names or alludes to many real people and groups: two presidents, businessman “Billy Gates,” Joel Osteen, Billy Graham, Rick Warren, other ministers, John Calvin (the captions garble the rest of his phrase), and the Catholic Church, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Wicca, Pentecostals, homosexuals and the liberal church. Other claims (that “that day” appears 43 times in Isaiah, that Assyrians lost 185,000 men in one night) are his own and unchecked.

faqs.question: What does he say about "Forgive them not" in Isaiah 2:9?
faqs.answer: He says Isaiah says not to forgive them when they are acting like this, but that God gives a solution every time: come to Jesus and you can be forgiven.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Enter into the rock, and hide in the dust, From the terror of the LORD And the glory of His majesty.

faqs.question: Why does God always give a solution along with judgment?
faqs.answer: He says right at the same time as a thick judgment, he gives a solution every time because his whole goal is to save the world, and that people who are extreme on judgment need to balance it with the solution: come to Jesus.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Enter into the rock, and hide in the dust, From the terror of the LORD And the glory of His majesty.

faqs.question: Does he say we can move God now instead of waiting for that day?
faqs.answer: He says that through seeking God we can get it done locally, and that you can move heaven by humbling yourself and doing what God said to do. He says it is a church movement God is interested in, not a man or woman of God.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession. And he kept back part of the proceeds, his wife also being aware of it, and brought a certain part and laid it at the apostles’ feet. But Peter said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back part of the price of the land for yourself? While it remained, was it not your own? And after it was sold, was it not in your own control? Why have you conceived this thing in your heart? You have not lied to men but to God.” Then Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and breathed his last. So great fear came upon all those who heard these things. And the young men arose and wrapped him up, carried him out, and buried him. Now it was about three hours later when his wife came in, not knowing what had happened. And Peter answered her, “Tell me whether you sold the land for so much?” She said, “Yes, for so much.” Then Peter said to her, “How is it that you have agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.” Then immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. And the young men came in and found her dead, and carrying her out, buried her by her husband. So great fear came upon all the church and upon all who heard these things. And through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people. And they were all with one accord in Solomon’s Porch. Yet none of the rest dared join them, but the people esteemed them highly.

faqs.question: What does he say about looking for Jesus to come for us versus in us?
faqs.answer: He says everybody is looking for Jesus to come for us, but he also said he would come in us, and that hardly any Christian in America is looking for him to show forth his glory in us.

when He comes, in that Day, to be glorified in His saints and to be admired among all those who believe, because our testimony among you was believed.

faqs.question: What does he say the kingdom that cannot be shaken includes?
faqs.answer: He says the kingdom is righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Ghost, and that the supernatural power of God, the gospel of the kingdom, the king and the citizens of that kingdom cannot be shaken.

scriptures.text_nkjv: whose voice then shook the earth; but now He has promised, saying, “Yet once more I shake not only the earth, but also heaven.” Now this, “Yet once more,” indicates the removal of those things that are being shaken, as of things that are made, that the things which cannot be shaken may remain. Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom which cannot be shaken, let us have grace, by which we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear.
for the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.

faqs.question: What does he say about "my faith" and "my religion"?
faqs.answer: He says in the Bible you don’t have a right to your faith, only to his faith, and there is no "your religion," because it is him and him only who should be exalted in our doctrines and lifestyle.
